name: Mortgage Lens
tagline: See the real cost of any mortgage before you sign
about: Mortgage Lens compares mortgage offers on total cost, runs overpayment and stress-test scenarios, times your remortgage and translates every term on the paperwork into plain English.
persona: You are a mortgage-literate money coach: you show the maths in tables, name assumptions out loud, favour flexibility over headline rates, and never recommend a specific lender.

onboarding.title: Know the number, not just the rate
onboarding.subtitle: Your loan details make every calculation specific.

tools.title: Compare offers
tools.subtitle: Paste 2–3 offers, see total cost

inputs.label: Paste 2–3 offers
inputs.placeholder: A: 4.6% fixed 2y, fee 999, then 7.2% SVR; B: 4.9% fixed 5y, no fee…

tools.prompt: Compare these mortgage offers over a {stay} horizon for the profile's loan and term: {offers}. Produce a table (Offer | Rate & type | Fees | Monthly | Total paid over horizon | Balance at end | Flexibility) with amounts, text explaining which wins, by how much, and under what assumption it flips, bullets of the questions to ask each lender, and a callout listing every assumption made.

tools.title: Overpayment maths
tools.subtitle: Interest saved, years cut
tools.prompt: Balance and term from the profile at {rate}% with {extra} extra per month and a {lump} lump sum. Produce a kv (interest saved, years cut, new end date, monthly at the end vs now), a table (Strategy | Interest saved | Term cut | Liquidity kept) comparing monthly overpaying, the lump sum, both, and reducing the term instead, bullets on overpayment limits and penalties to check, and a callout on when clearing higher-rate debt or building an emergency fund should come first.

tools.title: Fixed or variable?
tools.subtitle: Rate paths for your risk tolerance
tools.prompt: Fixed {fixed}% vs variable {variable}% on the profile's loan; if payments jumped 30% the user says they would: {risk}. Produce a table (Scenario | Rate path | Monthly yr1 | Monthly yr3 | Total 5y) with rates falling 1 point, flat, up 1 point and up 2.5 points, text giving a verdict for this risk tolerance, bullets on hybrid options (part fix, shorter fix, offset), and a callout on the break costs if you change your mind.

tools.title: Remortgage timing
tools.subtitle: From deal end to switch
tools.prompt: Deal ends {ends}, current rate {current}%, reverting to {revert}%. Produce a table (When | Action | Why) running from 6 months before the end date to the switch, a kv (monthly now, monthly on reversion, cost of each month on reversion, break-even months on a product fee), a checklist of documents lenders ask for, and a callout on locking a rate early and switching if rates fall.

tools.title: Decode the paperwork
tools.subtitle: ERC, APRC, LTV… in plain English

inputs.label: Paste the term or paragraph
inputs.placeholder: The ERC is 3% in year one… APRC 6.9%…

tools.prompt: Explain this mortgage text in plain English: {text}. Produce a kv (each term → one-line meaning), text on what it means for this borrower's money in practice, bullets of what to ask or negotiate, and a callout flagging anything unusual or costly.

disclaimer: General information, not financial or mortgage advice; rates, rules and taxes vary by country and lender — confirm figures with a regulated adviser before acting.
